excerpt: Everything you need to plan a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari: what happens on the morning, where balloons launch, realistic prices, the best months and honest tips.
content:
A Masai Mara hot air balloon safari is a sunrise flight of about one hour over the reserve's plains and the Mara River, followed by a cooked bush breakfast with sparkling wine where you land. Expect a 04:30 wake-up, a published price of roughly US$450-600 per adult, and a minimum age of 8.

The flight is easy to book but hard to judge from brochures. Which launch site suits your camp, how early you really start, what the ticket includes and whether it is worth it in your month all affect how good the morning feels. This guide answers those questions honestly from our base in Nairobi, so you can decide whether to add it to your Mara stay.

Photo by David Clode on Unsplash

Quick Facts

  • Flight time: About 45-60 minutes, launching at dawn
  • Wake-up: Around 04:30; back at camp by late morning
  • Price: Roughly US$450-600 per adult, shared basket (published rates, checked October 2026)
  • Includes: Transfer from nearby camps, flight, cooked breakfast with sparkling wine
  • Minimum age: 8 years and 1.2 m tall; no expectant mothers
  • Best months: July-October for the migration; all year in good weather
  • Main launch area: North-western Mara near the Mara River; other operators launch elsewhere

What Happens on a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari?

A Masai Mara hot air balloon safari follows the same rhythm almost every day: a dark start, an inflation at first light, an hour drifting with the wind, then breakfast in the grass and a game drive back. The outing takes around six hours and replaces your usual morning drive.

Before dawn: wake-up and transfer

Most camps knock on your tent with tea or coffee at about 04:30. Your driver or the balloon company then takes you to the launch site, which can be a few minutes or close to an hour away depending on where you stay. Wear warm layers: the Mara is around 1,500 metres above sea level and mornings are chilly.

Inflation, briefing and take-off

At the launch site the crew lays the envelopes out and fills them with cold air before the burners heat it. Your pilot gives a safety briefing, including the landing position you hold for touchdown. Guests climb into a divided wicker basket and lift off as the sky turns gold, which is the best light of the day for photographs.

The flight and the champagne breakfast

Balloons drift with the wind at heights that change through the flight, from just above the treetops to a few hundred metres up. After landing, the ground crew sets up a full cooked breakfast with sparkling wine on the plains, then your guide drives you back to camp with a game drive along the way. Some operators also hand out a flight certificate.

Where Do Balloons Launch in the Masai Mara?

Balloons launch from several sites across the Masai Mara, and the one you use depends mainly on where your camp is. The longest-running operator, flying since 1978, uses a single sheltered launch site beside Little Governors' Camp in the north-west of the reserve, close to the Mara River.

Photo by David Clode on Unsplash

According to Governors Balloon Safaris, on about 95 days in every 100 the wind carries their balloons south over the Mara River and its riverine forest and then across the open plains of the Mara Triangle. That route gives a good chance of seeing hippos and crocodiles in the river, plus elephants, buffalo and plains game below.

Other licensed balloon companies launch from different parts of the reserve and some neighbouring areas, so camps in the central and eastern Mara have their own options. If you are staying in a private conservancy, ask whether a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari is available from your camp and how long the transfer is; a very long pre-dawn drive can make the morning feel rushed. Our guide to the Masai Mara reserve versus the conservancies explains how location shapes your whole stay.

How Much Does a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari Cost?

A Masai Mara hot air balloon safari costs roughly US$450-600 per adult in a shared basket, based on published rates. Children usually pay less, and private baskets for families or groups cost several thousand dollars. Prices rise in the peak migration months, so the same flight can cost more in August than in March.

These figures are estimates built from published rates; for example, one Mara lodge lists US$530 standard and US$580 peak for adults, and US$330 for children aged 8-15 (2025 rates, checked October 2026). Ask whether your quote includes the transfer, breakfast, any conservancy fee and VAT, and confirm the current price before you book.

When Is the Best Time for a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari?

The best time for a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari is July to October, when the wildebeest migration is usually in the Mara and the plains below are full of herds. Flights run all year, though, and January to March offers dry weather, green-gold grass and fewer vehicles at a lower price.

Photo by Alan Wouda on Unsplash

MonthsWhat you see from the basketFlying conditions
July-OctoberMigration herds, river crossings in the area, big cats on the plainsDry and usually calm; busiest and dearest
November-DecemberResident wildlife and green plains after the short rainsSome showers; most mornings fly
January-MarchPlains game, elephants and predators on drier grassGenerally dry; good value
April-MayLush green landscapes, fewer visitorsLong rains; more weather cancellations
JuneGrass turning gold as herds start to arriveCooling and drying out

Migration timing shifts with the rains every year, so a balloon flight does not guarantee herds or a crossing beneath you. Read our guide to Mara migration timing and our month-by-month advice on the best time to visit the Masai Mara before you choose your dates.

Is a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari Worth It?

A Masai Mara hot air balloon safari is worth it if you want a once-in-a-lifetime view of the Mara's scale and dawn light and the price fits. It is less worth it on a short stay, if you hate early starts, or if you would rather fund an extra night.

Who it suits

Honeymooners, photographers who want aerial landscapes, and anyone on a three-night or longer Mara stay tend to love a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari. From the basket you understand how the river, the forest and the open grassland fit together, something you never see from a vehicle.

Honest trade-offs

You will not get close-up wildlife photographs from the air; animals are small at height and the balloon cannot stop or turn back for a sighting. You also give up your best morning game drive. On a two-night stay we often suggest saving the flight for a return trip and focusing on drives instead.

Photo by Edmar Gonçalves on Unsplash

If you are comparing balloon flights in several parks, our broader hot air balloon safari guide covers options across East Africa, including the Serengeti, while this page stays focused on the Masai Mara.

How Do You Book and Prepare for a Masai Mara Balloon Flight?

You book a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari through your safari planner or your camp, ideally when you confirm your accommodation. Seats are limited and are matched to the morning you are near a launch site, so booking months ahead for July to October avoids disappointment.

What to wear and bring

For a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari, dress in layers you can remove as the sun rises: a fleece or warm jacket, long trousers and closed shoes for the walk through damp grass. A hat that will not blow off, a camera with a wide-to-medium zoom and a spare battery are useful. Leave large bags at camp, because space in the basket is tight.

Safety, health and weather

Pilots will not fly in strong wind or rain, and the decision is made on the morning. If a flight is cancelled, operators normally offer another morning or a refund, but confirm the terms when you book. Landings can be bumpy, so anyone pregnant, with back or neck problems, or with limited mobility should check with the operator first. Good travel insurance is sensible for any safari.

Getting to the Mara

The Masai Mara is about 275 km from Nairobi, roughly five and a half hours by road, or a short scheduled flight from Wilson Airport. Fly-in guests sometimes take the balloon on their first or last morning, so tell your planner your flight times. Our Kenya safari packages combine the Mara with Amboseli, Lake Naivasha and other parks, and the 6-day Best of Amboseli and Masai Mara Safari has the balloon as an optional extra.

Insider Tips

  • Pick the right night: Schedule the flight for a morning when you are staying close to the launch site, not on a travel day
  • Ask about transfer time: A short pre-dawn drive means more sleep and a calmer start
  • Shoot wide: Landscape shots and balloon shadows on the grass work better than distant animals
  • Eat lightly: Have a biscuit with your early tea; the full breakfast comes after landing
  • Plan a spare morning: On a three-night stay, a cancelled flight can often move to the next day
  • Check inclusions: Confirm transfer, breakfast, fees and VAT so there are no surprises

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari cost?

A Masai Mara hot air balloon safari usually costs US$450-600 per adult in a shared basket. One Mara lodge publishes US$530 in standard season and US$580 in peak season, with children aged 8 to 15 at US$330 (2025 rates, checked October 2026). Confirm the current price before booking.

How long is the balloon flight over the Masai Mara?

The flight itself on a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari lasts about 45 minutes to one hour, depending on wind. The whole outing takes far longer: a wake-up around 04:30, a pre-dawn transfer, the flight, a cooked breakfast where you land and a game drive back, so most guests return to camp by late morning.

Is there an age limit for a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari?

Yes. The longest-running operator in the reserve requires children to be at least 8 years old and taller than 1.2 metres, and expectant mothers cannot fly. Landings can be bumpy, so anyone with back, neck or joint problems, or limited mobility, should check with their doctor and the operator before booking.

When is the best time for a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari?

A Masai Mara hot air balloon safari runs all year, but July to October is the most popular time because the wildebeest migration fills the plains below. January to March is drier and quieter. In the long rains of April and May some mornings are cancelled for weather, though flights still operate when conditions allow.

Do I need to book the balloon in advance?

Booking a Masai Mara hot air balloon safari in advance is strongly recommended, especially from July to October and over Christmas, when baskets fill weeks ahead. Each balloon carries a limited number of guests, and the flight must be matched to the nights you spend near a launch site. We can reserve it when we confirm your Masai Mara camp.

Final Thoughts

A Masai Mara hot air balloon safari gives you an hour of silence over the plains at sunrise, a bush breakfast and a view of the Mara that no game drive can match. Budget roughly US$450-600 per adult, book early for July to October and choose a morning when you are staying near a launch site.
